families.description: Authentication posture, auth-context visibility, provider-auth adapter posture, and future device-login contracts
families.notes: Canonical auth family. Auth is not session. Provider session is not YAI session. Auth does not own entitlement, machine authorization, license lease, runtime gate, case, operator context, client attachment, or shell attachment. Runtime-facing access projection is consumed by ../yai/src/runtime/access; this does not create a native identity plane. `auth.whoami` remains deprecated compatibility only.

families.description: Principal, machine, entitlement, and authorization posture
families.notes: Public API identity family for principal, machine, entitlement, and authorization projection grammar. It is upstream/API-owned and projects bounded access posture to ../yai/src/runtime/access; it must not imply ../yai/src/identity or a native identity plane.

families.description: Legacy client-session compatibility contracts retained for migration only
families.notes: Legacy compatibility family only. Session is not a canonical domain family in V51; canonical public meaning is split across auth, case/context, shell/client, and system status surfaces.

families.description: Connected client visibility and permissions projections
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: System/runtime status and diagnostics projections
families.notes: Canonical system/runtime diagnostic family. Runtime lifecycle control actions such as start/stop/restart remain forbidden as canonical domain operations.

families.description: Case tree, root, open/close, and case inspection contracts with operator-context projections retained for CLI compatibility
families.notes: Canonical public case family. Case is not session. Active case belongs to operator context. `case.enter`, `case.leave`, and `case.status` remain valid public projections, but explicit API ownership of `active_case_ref` is now expressed by the `operator_context` family. `case.close` closes a case-tree entry only and must not imply evidence, knowledge, or records deletion by default. Older `case.create` and `case.use` naming remains compatibility-only.

families.description: Operator-context posture and active-case selection contracts
families.notes: Canonical API family for active-case selection posture. Operator context owns `active_case_ref`. It does not own auth, authorization, runtime lifecycle, jobs, workflows, agents, provider/model execution, records, evidence, knowledge, analytics, client connection, or shell lifecycle.

families.description: Conversation lifecycle, messages, and intent/context linkage
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: Prompt context assembly and future template, preview, and trace contracts distinct from conversation and execution families
families.notes: Public operation grammar family. `prompting.context.assemble` is the current partial canonical operation; template/preview/trace render or replay surfaces remain planned and must not imply model, provider, or agent execution.

families.description: Workflow composition, validation, execution, and watch contracts
families.notes: Canonical API family. `flow` remains a legacy compatibility alias only and must not be reintroduced as a canonical family. Runtime implementation ownership maps to ../yai/src/orchestrator/workflow.

families.description: Governance posture, policy resolution, decisions, and obligations
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: Control-plane subject/boundary/gate/evidence operations
families.notes: Control remains canonical for gates and decisions. Evidence inspection may project through a first-class `evidence` family while `control.evidence.*` is retained only for compatibility.

families.description: Knowledge query, context, lineage, graph, and memory promotion
families.notes: Knowledge remains a public API family, but V51 also promotes lineage and recall as first-class families. `knowledge.lineage.*` remains compatibility-only when lineage is first-class.

families.description: State snapshots, diffs, and record query/tail contracts
families.notes: Canonical semantic state family. `state.records.*` is canonical over any hypothetical root `records.*` family.

families.description: Skill registry, admissibility, execution, and proof obligations
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: Provider inventory, selection, connectivity, and probe operations
families.notes: Canonical plural API family. CLI/TUI projections may use singular `provider` without changing the API family name.

families.description: Model inventory, selection, capability inspection, and evaluation
families.notes: Canonical plural API family. CLI/TUI projections may use singular `model` without changing the API family name.

families.description: Agent listing, planning, execution, and tracing
families.notes: Canonical plural API family. CLI/TUI projections may use singular `agent` without changing the API family name.

families.description: Planning, routing, handoff, and recovery orchestration
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: Analytics query, report, workflow summary, and gate analysis
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: Output listing, preview, render, and export contracts
families.notes: Public operation grammar family; runtime implementation is in ../yai/src/runtime/boundary/api handlers.

families.description: Policy-pack inventory, inspection, validation, and explanation projections
families.notes: Canonical API family spelling uses underscore. CLI/TUI projections may render `policy-pack` while the API family remains `policy_pack`.

families.description: Governed intake planning, execution, status, outputs, and lineage projections
families.notes: Intake is a first-class API family in V51 and must not be collapsed into generic query or knowledge surfaces.

families.description: Materialization planning, execution, outputs, evidence, and lineage projections
families.notes: Canonical API family spelling is `materialization`. CLI/TUI projections may use `materialize` while the API family remains noun-based.

families.description: Case-bound excerpt listing, inspection, and lineage projections
families.notes: Excerpts are case-bound materialization outputs and must not be treated as free-floating documents.

families.description: Evidence listing, inspection, and lineage projections
families.notes: Evidence is promoted to a first-class API family in V51. `control.evidence.*` remains compatibility-only where retained.

families.description: First-class lineage trace, explain, show, and graph projections
families.notes: Lineage becomes a first-class API family in V51 rather than remaining buried entirely under `knowledge.lineage.*`.

families.description: Governed recall query, explain, and inspect projections
families.notes: Recall is governed and case-bound. Root query remains forbidden as a standalone semantic owner.

families.description: Job planning, start, status, logs, outputs, evidence, and lineage projections
families.notes: Job becomes an explicit public API family in V51 instead of remaining an under-modeled runtime concept.

families.description: License posture, lease status, cache status, and safe check projections
families.notes: License remains posture/projection only. Billing or subscription truth does not move into this family. Runtime-facing consumption projects through ../yai/src/runtime/access, not a native identity plane.

families.description: Machine posture, identity status, evidence status, and authorization projections
families.notes: Machine projections must remain safe and must not expose raw hardware, fingerprint, or secret material. Runtime-facing machine authorization posture projects through ../yai/src/runtime/access.

families.description: Shared-account limits posture and explanation projections
families.notes: Limits remains a safe projection family and must not become quota-ledger or billing truth. Runtime gate consumption projects through ../yai/src/runtime/access where access posture is required.

families.description: Scoped runtime, job, workflow, agent, and provider log-watch projections
families.notes: Logs is scoped only. Generic root log ownership is forbidden; each log surface must remain attached to an explicit subject.
